title: A young person's seva
hook: the first seva a young person chooses
tomorrow: an amrit sign-up sheet. how would Simran know she's ready?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a sandalwood tree and a line from Proverbs, both saying the same thing about friends: good company. Leo said maybe. Today Fateh says yes to something on his own.

At a big Sunday gathering, the gurdwara's coordinator holds up a clipboard: who wants a job? Rotis, dishes, the water line, the shoe racks. Last week the adults handed Fateh a pitcher. This week nobody hands him anything. He's been told he can pick. Simran expects the kitchen, where the action is. Instead Fateh walks straight to the shoe racks by the door, where an old man is setting out pairs, and asks if he can help.
screen: `WHO WANTS A JOB?` → `NOBODY HANDS HIM ANYTHING.` → `FATEH PICKS THE SHOE RACKS.`

segments.voice: Seva is selfless service, and the Granth puts it right in the middle of ordinary life. On ang 26, Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: serve here, in the midst of the world, and you'll be given a seat of honor in the Lord's court. Not away from the world. In it, at the door, with the shoes. Children in langar are handed jobs. The first seva a young person chooses is different: nobody assigned it, so it's theirs. Fateh says he picked the shoes because the old man looked like he could use a friend. Good company again. And Simran makes her choice the same night. She writes back to the camp director: yes, one week, move-in or not. Two first choices in one family. Now the last six days come back in one breath. Honest answers: nobody knows that, and here's what I do know. Crowned, by your own hands. Their own sikhi, by keeping and by asking. Calm courage: frighten no one, fear no one. Learning together. Good company, like sandalwood.
screen: `SEVA: SELFLESS SERVICE.` · `ANG 26: SERVE IN THE WORLD.` · `ASSIGNED, THEN CHOSEN.` · `TWO FIRST CHOICES.` · then, large: `THE FIRST SEVA.`

segments.voice: Look at your own hands, palms up, for a full minute. Remember the jobs they've been handed, and of one they might choose: something small that no one would ask of you. Then let them rest and sit with that choice.
A young person's seva. The first service a young Sikh chooses, instead of being handed.
The first seva: nobody assigned it, so it belongs to the one who chose it. Two weeks, done.

screen: `DAY 1652 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 26 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: AN AMRIT SIGN-UP SHEET. HOW WOULD SHE KNOW SHE'S READY?`

howItsDone: Young Sikhs may begin seva at the gurdwara with jobs handed to them, then choose their own: the kitchen, the dishes, the water line, or the shoe racks by the door.
